rationale: A wins because it keeps the core tension reporter-grade without inventing legal facts: "The undisclosed terms are the reporting hook, not a footnote" is exactly the right media-business spine. B has sharper instincts in places, but "Perplexity starts paying publishers it was being sued over" turns legal threats into lawsuits, and "Perplexity is now paid twice on the same answer" states an inference before the terms exist. That is how a useful angle becomes a correction waiting to happen.
gaps_in_A: "after months of legal threats" adds a timeline the update does not give. The legal-threat fact is real; the duration is decoration.
"live criticism and legal threats" overstates the present-tense status. The update says Perplexity has faced them, not that they are active today.
The set misses the clean data angle around "hundreds of millions of queries a month" versus undisclosed publisher payouts. That arithmetic hole is reporter-shaped.
"recent multi-billion raise makes the monetization question current" is viable but thin without the valuation, round date, or a revenue number.
gaps_in_B: "was being sued over" is invented. The update says criticism and legal threats, not lawsuits.
"offering those same publishers a cut" asserts the threatened publishers are eligible or participating. The facts do not say that.
"Perplexity is now paid twice on the same answer" is a sharp question, but a bad headline. Same-answer overlap and referral-revenue exclusion are not established.
"attempt to settle out of court with product features" is legal-theater phrasing without suit or settlement facts behind it.
